issuing_body: High Court of Delhi
summary: A series of Delhi High Court orders in 2026 recognised that personality and publicity rights protect name, image, voice and likeness against AI deepfakes, while refusing blanket injunctions and distinguishing satire from vulgar or commercial misuse. key_provisions: Personality rights protect name, image, voice, likeness and other indicia against AI and deepfake misuse (Devi Prasad Shetty v. Medicine Me, 2026:DHC:8897); Courts consistently order removal of sexually explicit AI content but refuse blanket injunctions; claimants must show monetisation, not mere popularity (Bhambhani J); Raghav Chadha: six vulgar AI posts ordered removed; political satire left online; Shashi Tharoor: X directed to remove AI deepfake video; voice and speaking style protected; Amitabh Bachchan v. Rajat Nagi (5 Nov 2026, Kaurav J): permanent injunction; two-step test of validity and identifiability; Amici curiae appointed to address scope of personality rights; detailed hearings scheduled October 2026
confidence_note: Case facts from MediaNama, SCC Online, Verdictum and LiveLaw Biz; exact dates of several interim orders are approximate (month). Jurisdiction coded DL because the issuing court is the Delhi High Court, though the rulings are relied on nationally.

key_provisions: Free AI courses for Classes VI-XII; Students to earn national certification on completion; State AI policy announced in March 2026; adoption status in the window not confirmed
confidence_note: Telegraph India headline only; course order and whether the March 2026 state AI policy was adopted not verified.

title: Copyright Act, 1957 (as applied to AI training and outputs)
issuing_body: Parliament of India / DPIIT
summary: The copyright statute, with no AI-specific provision. Section 52(1)(a)(i) (fair dealing for private or personal use including research) was held prima facie to cover LLM training in ANI v OpenAI; s. 2(d)(vi) treats the person who causes a computer-generated work to be created as its author. Amendment proposals from the DPIIT committee are pending.
key_provisions: s. 2(d)(vi): author of a computer-generated literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work is 'the person who causes the work to be created'; s. 52(1)(a)(i): fair dealing for private or personal use including research; relied on by Delhi HC (interim) for training-stage copying; s. 14 and s. 51: reproduction and storage rights; infringement; ss. 31C-31D statutory licences cited by DPIIT committee as model for an AI-training licence; No amendment introduced in Parliament as of Nov 2026 despite July 2026 reports of a draft
confidence_note: Statutory provisions from standard knowledge of the Act; the copyright.gov.in URL is the standard location of the Act text but was not fetched this session.

title: Information Technology Act, 2000
issuing_body: Parliament of India / MeitY
summary: The principal statute for cyber offences, intermediary liability and government blocking powers. It is technology-neutral and is the legal basis for the 2021 Intermediary Rules and the 2026 synthetic-media amendments; the Government's stated position is that it already applies to AI systems.
key_provisions: s. 66C identity theft and s. 66D cheating by personation using a computer resource (up to 3 years and Rs 1 lakh fine) used against deepfake impersonation; s. 66E violation of privacy (capturing/publishing private-area images), s. 67/67A/67B obscene, sexually explicit and child sexual abuse material; s. 69A blocking of public access to information, with the 2009 Blocking Rules; s. 79 safe harbour for intermediaries conditional on due diligence; s. 79(3)(b) loss of immunity on failure to act on 'actual knowledge' via government or court notice; s. 87 rule-making power used for the IT Rules 2021 and the 2026 SGI amendments
confidence_note: Statute well known; the 27th Standing Committee report (Mar 2026) records MeitY's position that the IT Act is technology-neutral and applies to AI.

title: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 Artificial Intelligence (BIS participation)
issuing_body: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS, LITD 30 mirror committee) / ISO/IEC JTC 1
summary: India participates through BIS in the ISO/IEC subcommittee that develops international AI standards (terminology, trustworthiness, risk management, ISO/IEC 42001), mirrored domestically by BIS committee LITD 30.
key_provisions: BIS is understood to be a participating (P) member of SC 42 with a national mirror committee (LITD 30) that adopts SC 42 standards as Indian Standards (general knowledge); SC 42 outputs include ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems), ISO/IEC 23894 (AI risk management) and ISO/IEC 22989 (concepts and terminology); Quad Principles on CET standards and the TTC standards work stream reference this process
confidence_note: iso.org participation page returned 403; P-member status and LITD 30 role from general knowledge only.

title: Bureau of Indian Standards LITD 30 (Artificial Intelligence) standards, including IS/ISO/IEC 42001:2023
issuing_body: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Electronics and IT Division Council, Sectional Committee LITD 30
summary: BIS's AI committee adopts ISO/IEC SC 42 standards as Indian Standards. Adopted standards include IS/ISO/IEC 22989 (terminology), 23053 (ML framework), 23894 (AI risk management) and 42001:2023 (AI management system). All are voluntary unless referenced in a Quality Control Order or regulation, which has not happened for AI.
key_provisions: LITD 30 set up in 2018; members from industry, academia, MeitY, NITI Aayog; mirrors ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42; IS/ISO/IEC 42001:2023 adopted as the Indian AI management-system standard (certifiable, voluntary); Foundational standards adopted: IS/ISO/IEC 22989:2022, IS/ISO/IEC 23053:2022; risk management IS/ISO/IEC 23894; BIS 2024 handbook counts 61 standards published or under consideration across foundational, data, trustworthiness and governance themes; other sources cite 22 published; No AI standard made mandatory via Quality Control Order as of Nov 2026; MeitY's Nov 2025 governance guidelines reference BIS/TEC standards as voluntary compliance tools
confidence_note: BIS handbook PDF (Sept 2024) read via text extraction and confirms LITD 30 (2018), 42001 adoption and '61 standards'. Counts differ between sources (22 vs 61). The March 2026 'ethical AI' standards report is a single secondary source without standard numbers; no 2026 'National Standard for AI' from MeitY was located.

title: Report of the Task Force on Strategic Implementation of AI for National Security and Defence
issuing_body: Ministry of Defence, Department of Defence Production
summary: Government-commissioned task force report that recommended the institutional architecture for military AI, leading to the Defence AI Council and Defence AI Project Agency in 2019.
key_provisions: Recommended a Defence AI Council for policy and a Defence AI Project Agency for execution; Recommended dedicated funding and AI roadmaps for the services and defence PSUs; Report text not public in full; recommendations known through MoD statements
confidence_note: Dates and outcome consistent across think-tank sources; the task force chair (widely reported as N. Chandrasekaran, Tata Sons) was not confirmed by the sources read.

title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence #AIforAll
issuing_body: NITI Aayog
summary: Discussion paper identifying five priority sectors for AI and proposing a research-institution network and policy enablers.
key_provisions: Five focus sectors: healthcare, agriculture, education, smart cities and infrastructure, smart mobility and transportation; Proposed Centres of Research Excellence (COREs) and International Centres of Transformational AI (ICTAIs); Identified barriers: data ecosystems, compute, skills, IP and privacy; proposed a national AI marketplace; Framed India as an 'AI garage' for developing-country solutions
confidence_note: Document and date well established; URL from prior knowledge, not re-fetched this session.

title: National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS)
issuing_body: Union Cabinet; Department of Science and Technology
summary: DST mission funding 25 Technology Innovation Hubs at academic institutions in cyber-physical technologies including AI and machine learning.
key_provisions: Outlay ₹3,660 crore over five years; 25 Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs) as Section 8 companies, several AI-focused (e.g. iHub Drishti at IIT Jodhpur for computer vision/AR-VR; TIH at IIT Kharagpur for AI in agriculture); Covers technology development, HRD and skills, innovation and start-ups, and international collaboration; Hubs later partner in IndiaAI Safe & Trusted projects
confidence_note: Cabinet date and outlay from prior knowledge of the PIB release; URL not re-fetched this session.

title: CBSE Artificial Intelligence skill subject (Code 417 for Classes IX-X; Code 843 for Classes XI-XII)
issuing_body: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)
summary: Optional AI skill subject in CBSE schools with curricula and handbooks for Classes IX-XII and subject-integration manuals; the earlier, elective layer beneath the 2026 compulsory CT&AI curriculum.
key_provisions: Skill subject code 417 (Classes IX-X) and 843 (Classes XI-XII) with annual curriculum documents and handbooks on cbseacademic.nic.in; Integration manuals for teaching AI through Hindi, English, Mathematics, Science and Social Science; Optional for schools and students; not a central mandate
confidence_note: CBSE page confirms subject codes and resources, but introduction years (2019-20, 2020-21) are from memory and were not verified in this session.

title: Reporting for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) applications and systems offered and used by market intermediaries / MIIs / mutual funds
issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
summary: SEBI circulars requiring intermediaries, exchanges/depositories and mutual funds to file a quarterly AI/ML reporting form describing AI/ML systems offered to investors or used internally.
key_provisions: Quarterly AI/ML Reporting Form to be submitted within 15 days of quarter end (via exchanges/depositories for intermediaries); Covers applications offered to investors or used internally for investing, trading, advice dissemination and all fintech/regtech initiatives using AI/ML; Stated objectives: inventory AI/ML use, confirm compliance with SEBI cyber security framework, and record safeguards against data breach and system failure; Still the only SEBI AI-specific obligation in force as of November 2026; a wider framework is pending (see 2025 consultation)
confidence_note: Circular text read via NSDL-hosted copy (not sebi.gov.in). MII circular date of 31 Jan 2019 is from memory of secondary coverage and should be checked.

title: Defence AI Council (DAIC) and Defence AI Project Agency (DAIPA)
issuing_body: Ministry of Defence (executive order)
summary: Apex council chaired by the Defence Minister and an implementing agency under Secretary (Defence Production) to steer AI adoption across the armed forces and defence PSUs.
key_provisions: DAIC chaired by the Raksha Mantri; DAIPA headed ex officio by Secretary (Defence Production); Created by MoD executive order dated 8 Feb 2019 implementing the 2018 AI Task Force recommendations; AI roadmaps for each DPSU; PIB reports 61 projects under DPSUs with 30 completed; Annual AI budget earmarked for defence AI projects (reported as ₹100 crore per year for DPSUs over five years); AI groups embedded in DRDO laboratories
confidence_note: Executive order date and structure confirmed via PIB snippet and CSDR paper; the annual budget figure varies across sources (₹100 crore/yr vs ₹1,000 crore corpus) and is flagged as uncertain.

title: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (India non-adherent)
issuing_body: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (India: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, no adherence)
summary: The OECD AI Principles are the reference text for the G20 AI Principles that India has endorsed through G20 declarations, but India has not formally adhered to the OECD Recommendation itself.
key_provisions: Adherents are the 38 OECD members, the EU and non-members Argentina, Brazil, Egypt, Malta, Peru, Romania, Singapore and Ukraine; India is not listed; OECD page notes G20 members China, India, Indonesia, Russia, Saudi Arabia and South Africa are not adherents; India reaffirmed the G20 AI Principles (2019) in para 61 of the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration (Sept 2023); Principles revised May 2024 to address general-purpose and generative AI
confidence_note: oecd.ai adherents list read; India absent and explicitly named as a non-adhering G20 member.

title: National Automated Facial Recognition System (NAFRS) procurement
issuing_body: National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), Ministry of Home Affairs
summary: Long-running NCRB tender for a centralised police facial-recognition system; no statute authorises it and its operational status is unclear. Included as the central law-enforcement AI procurement of record.
key_provisions: Intended to match faces against CCTNS and other police databases for identification of suspects and missing persons; NCRB cited a 2009 Cabinet note on CCTNS as legal basis; MHA Rajya Sabha reply (April 2020) described it as a tool to facilitate better identification; Civil-society challenges (IFF, Panoptic) on absence of legal framework; no dedicated FRT law or MHA guidelines located; Current deployment status not verified as of Nov 2026
confidence_note: Tender chronology well documented to 2021; nothing found on award or operation in 2022-2026. Status recorded as 'announced'.

title: Code on Social Security, 2020 – gig and platform worker provisions
issuing_body: Ministry of Labour and Employment
summary: Central labour code that defines gig and platform workers and aggregators and creates a social security fund financed partly by aggregator contributions; it contains no provisions on algorithmic management or automated decision-making.
key_provisions: Statutory definitions of 'gig worker', 'platform worker' and 'aggregator' (Section 2); Section 114: aggregators in notified categories contribute 1-2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of amounts paid to gig and platform workers; Aggregators must share worker data electronically for registration and maintain payment records; No obligations on algorithmic transparency, rating systems or automated deactivation; those appear only in state laws (Rajasthan 2023, Karnataka 2025) covered by other researchers
confidence_note: Provisions confirmed via PRS and legal commentary; commencement date (Nov 2025) not verified in this session, so status recorded as 'adopted' rather than 'in-force'.

title: Responsible AI for All: Approach Document for India, Part 1 – Principles for Responsible AI
issuing_body: NITI Aayog
summary: Sets out seven principles for responsible AI in India derived from constitutional values.
key_provisions: Seven principles: safety and reliability; equality; inclusivity and non-discrimination; privacy and security; transparency; accountability; protection and reinforcement of positive human values; Distinguishes system considerations from societal considerations; Anchors principles in Article 14 and 21 jurisprudence
confidence_note: URL and date from prior knowledge (filename encodes 22 Feb 2021); not re-fetched.

title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
summary: Due-diligence rules that intermediaries must follow to retain safe harbour under s. 79 of the IT Act, plus a code of ethics for digital news publishers and OTT platforms. All deepfake and AI-content obligations on platforms have been inserted into these Rules by amendment.
key_provisions: Rule 3(1)(b): intermediaries must inform users not to host listed unlawful content categories and make reasonable efforts to prevent it; Rule 3(2)(b): removal within 24 hours (reduced to 2 hours in 2026) of non-consensual intimate or morphed imagery on complaint; Rule 4: additional obligations for Significant Social Media Intermediaries (50 lakh registered users), including Chief Compliance Officer, nodal contact, resident grievance officer, monthly compliance reports and first-originator traceability for messaging services; Part III: Code of Ethics and three-tier grievance mechanism for digital news publishers and OTT curated content; Rule 7: non-compliance removes the s. 79(1) exemption
confidence_note: Amendment dates (28 Oct 2022, 6 Apr 2023, 22 Oct 2025) are recorded in the 27th Standing Committee report. The MeitY PDF listed as source_url appears to be the consolidated Rules as amended in 2026 but returned HTTP 403 when fetched.

title: SUVAS and SUPACE – Supreme Court AI translation and research tools
issuing_body: Supreme Court of India (AI Committee / e-Committee)
summary: Internal Supreme Court AI tools for translating judgments into Indian languages (SUVAS) and for extracting facts and precedents to assist judges (SUPACE); operational tools rather than regulatory instruments.
key_provisions: SUVAS: machine translation of judgments into scheduled languages, later supplemented by Bhashini-based translation; SUPACE: AI assistant for case file analysis, expressly not used for decision-making; Governed administratively by the Supreme Court's AI Committee, which authored the 2026 draft regulations
confidence_note: Launch dates were not verified in this session (Wikipedia page not found; search budget exhausted). Brief entry for cross-reference only.

title: Responsible AI for All: Approach Document for India, Part 2 – Operationalizing Principles for Responsible AI
issuing_body: NITI Aayog
summary: Proposes mechanisms for government and private sector to operationalise the Part 1 principles.
key_provisions: Recommends a Council for Ethics and Technology / advisory body on AI ethics; Sectoral regulators to issue domain-specific guidance; self-assessment and third-party audits for private sector; Procurement standards and ethics-by-design for public AI systems; Capacity building for government officials and awareness for citizens
confidence_note: URL and date from prior knowledge; not re-fetched.

title: Digital India Bhashini (National Language Translation Mission)
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
summary: Central mission building open AI language models and APIs for 22 scheduled languages, used as digital public infrastructure by other ministries, courts and the agriculture chatbot. Owned by MeitY; recorded here as the DPI dependency for sectoral deployments.
key_provisions: Three-year mission (from July 2022) with an outlay of ₹495.51 crore; Provides translation, speech and OCR models through a public API and the Bhashini platform; Underpins sectoral uses including judgment translation and farmer advisories
confidence_note: Launch date and outlay from a Ministry of Finance post and IndiaAI; Cabinet approval note not retrieved. MeitY instruments are otherwise excluded from this file.

title: Responsible AI for All: Adopting the Framework – A Use Case Approach on Facial Recognition Technology
issuing_body: NITI Aayog
summary: Applies the Responsible AI principles to facial recognition technology, using DigiYatra as the illustrative case.
key_provisions: Distinguishes verification (1:1) from identification (1:N) uses and their risk profiles; Recommends legal basis, purpose limitation, accuracy testing and grievance redress for FRT deployments; Uses the DigiYatra airport system as the worked example; Calls for a dedicated FRT governance framework and oversight
confidence_note: URL and date from prior knowledge; not re-fetched.

title: Kisan e-Mitra AI chatbot (PM-KISAN, KCC and PMFBY queries)
issuing_body: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
summary: Voice-enabled AI chatbot run by the agriculture ministry answering scheme queries on PM-KISAN, Kisan Credit Card and PMFBY in 11 Indian languages.
key_provisions: Covers PM-KISAN, Kisan Credit Card and PMFBY; 11 regional languages; 93 lakh+ queries answered as of December 2025; Service deployment, no policy or data-governance text attached
confidence_note: Read from PIB backgrounder PDF.

title: YES-TECH and CROPIC: AI-enabled yield estimation and crop-loss assessment under PMFBY
issuing_body: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (PMFBY)
summary: PMFBY operational rules that give a minimum 30% weight to remote-sensing/AI yield estimates (YES-TECH) and use an AI photo-analysis tool (CROPIC) for localised calamity claims, affecting insurer payouts.
key_provisions: YES-TECH assigns a minimum 30 percent weightage to technology-based yield assessment in claim calculation; Adopted by nine states as of January 2025 (Madhya Pradesh fully technology-based, per PIB); CROPIC uses AI analysis of geotagged crop photographs for transparent loss assessment during localised calamities; Binding within the PMFBY scheme operational guidelines for participating states and insurers
confidence_note: 30% weightage, state adoption and CROPIC EOI read from PIB backgrounder; YES-TECH start year is approximate.

title: Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy (India non-endorser)
issuing_body: United States Department of State (India: Ministry of External Affairs / Ministry of Defence, not endorsed)
summary: US-led set of non-binding principles for military AI (human accountability, legal review, bias mitigation, safeguards). India has not endorsed.
key_provisions: Carnegie (Aug 2024) records India among states that did not endorse the Declaration; Endorsers numbered around 58 by 2024 (general knowledge); India absent; Declaration measures: legal reviews, senior-level oversight of high-consequence applications, auditable methodologies, bias minimisation; India instead stresses the CCW GGE's eleven guiding principles
confidence_note: State Department pages returned 403; India's non-endorsement from Carnegie (Aug 2024). No later evidence of India endorsing found.

title: Ethical Guidelines for Application of Artificial Intelligence in Biomedical Research and Healthcare
issuing_body: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Department of Health Research
summary: ICMR's first ethical framework for AI in health research and care, addressed to developers, researchers, clinicians, ethics committees, sponsors and funders.
key_provisions: Ten patient-centric principles including autonomy, safety and risk minimisation, trustworthiness, data privacy, accountability and liability, optimisation of data quality, accessibility and equity, collaboration, non-discrimination and fairness, validity; Requires ethics committee review of AI health research and clinical/field validation of AI tools before deployment; Addresses informed consent, data governance and sharing, and human oversight in diagnostic and prognostic AI; Non-binding guidance; enforcement operates through institutional ethics committees and ICMR funding conditions
confidence_note: ICMR page read and official PDF located; exact day of release not shown on the ICMR page (press coverage dated 27 March 2023). Principle list from MediaNama summary.

title: Digital India Act (proposed replacement for the IT Act, 2000)
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
summary: A long-promised statute to replace the IT Act 2000 with risk-based rules for digital platforms, intermediaries and 'high-risk' AI. No bill or public draft has been introduced in Parliament as of November 2026; the Government has instead amended the IT Rules and signalled a separate AI consultation paper.
key_provisions: 2023 consultation deck proposed regulating 'high-risk AI systems' through algorithmic accountability, risk assessment and vulnerability review; Proposed reconsidering blanket safe harbour for all intermediaries and classifying intermediaries by function; No draft text published since 2023; no bill introduced in Parliament through the Winter Session 2025 or Monsoon Session 2026; MeitY told the Standing Committee in 2026 that DIA is 'under formulation to replace the IT Act and introduce new central legal framework to deal with emerging issues of AI'
confidence_note: Status (no bill, no draft) consistent across MediaNama (Dec 2025, Jul 2026) and the Standing Committee record. The 2023 consultation dates are from recall of MeitY presentations and press, not re-verified this session.

title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2023
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
summary: Amendment that would have required intermediaries to remove content about the Central Government identified as 'fake or misleading' by a government Fact Check Unit, and that introduced self-regulatory bodies for online real-money gaming. The FCU clause was struck down by the Bombay High Court and the Union's appeal is pending in the Supreme Court.
key_provisions: Rule 3(1)(b)(v) extended to information 'in respect of any business of the Central Government' flagged by a notified Fact Check Unit; Online gaming: self-regulatory bodies to verify 'permissible online real money games'; KYC obligations for gaming intermediaries; FCU clause held unconstitutional by Bombay HC on 20 Sep 2024; FCU never operationalised; Supreme Court appeal (Union v Kunal Kamra) pending; notice issued March 2026, no stay
confidence_note: Gazette text not fetched; dates from Supreme Court Observer, IFF and news. Exact March 2026 date of SC notice not confirmed (month precision for that milestone).

title: EU-India Trade and Technology Council (Working Group 1 on strategic technologies, digital governance and AI)
issuing_body: Ministry of External Affairs / Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) with the European Commission
summary: Ministerial coordination body on trade and technology; Working Group 1 covers trustworthy AI, large language model research, digital public infrastructure, semiconductors and high-performance computing.
key_provisions: Three working groups: strategic technologies/digital governance/connectivity; green and clean energy; trade, investment and resilient value chains; AI work stream covers trustworthy AI, joint research on large language models and AI standards, and high-performance computing (general knowledge); Third ministerial (16 Jul 2026) reported progress on AI, semiconductors and supply-chain resilience (DD India, ANI, ET Government); EU and India opened talks on India's association to Horizon Europe (Jul 2026)
confidence_note: Both EC TTC pages tried returned 404; dates of the 2023 and 2025 ministerials and the AI work-stream content are from general knowledge; 2026 ministerial confirmed only by headlines. EU trade policy India page given as forum URL.

title: Quad AI-ENGAGE initiative and Quad Principles on Critical and Emerging Technology Standards
issuing_body: Ministry of External Affairs / Quad (Australia, India, Japan, United States)
summary: Quad commitments on AI through an agriculture research initiative (AI-ENGAGE) and principles for standards development in critical and emerging technologies, endorsed by India.
key_provisions: Quad Principles on Critical and Emerging Technology Standards support 'industry-led, consensus-based multi-stakeholder approaches' to standards (20 May 2023); AI-ENGAGE (Advancing Innovations for Empowering NextGen Agriculture) funds joint research using AI, robotics and sensing for farmers across the Indo-Pacific; Wilmington Declaration announces 'an inaugural $7.5+ million in funding opportunities for joint research' under AI-ENGAGE; Quad BioExplore Initiative: funded mechanism for 'joint AI-driven exploration of diverse non-human biological data'; Forthcoming Quad Principles for Research and Development Collaborations in Critical and Emerging Technologies
confidence_note: Both archived White House texts read. The 2023 statement itself does not name AI-ENGAGE; the 2024 text says it was 'announced at last year's Summit' (via a fact sheet). MEA copies not fetched.

title: TEC Standard 57050:2023 - Fairness Assessment and Rating of Artificial Intelligence Systems
issuing_body: Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), Department of Telecommunications
summary: A voluntary TEC standard providing a procedure to assess and rate the fairness of AI systems, aimed at telecom and ICT deployments but drafted to be sector-agnostic. It uses a three-step method: bias risk assessment across the AI lifecycle, selection of fairness metrics and thresholds, and quantitative bias testing producing a Bias Index and Fairness Score.
key_provisions: Step 1: survey-based bias risk assessment across seven lifecycle stages on a five-point scale; Step 2: questionnaire to fix system intent, protected attributes, stakeholders and mandatory fairness metrics with threshold values; Step 3: group fairness metrics (statistical parity difference, disparate impact, equal opportunity difference, average odds difference, equalised odds) aggregated into a Bias Index and Fairness Score/rating; Voluntary; cited by MeitY's 2025 AI governance guidelines and the Standing Committee as an available assurance tool; TEC has also issued related work on AI robustness assessment (not verified in this session)
confidence_note: Standard number and method confirmed by two secondary sources; tec.gov.in PDF URL not retrieved. One secondary source describes compliance as a 'prerequisite for deployment' in telecom, which conflicts with the generally voluntary character of TEC standards; treated as voluntary absent a DoT mandate. Release month approximate.

title: Recommendations on Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Big Data in Telecommunication Sector
issuing_body: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)
summary: TRAI's statutory recommendations to DoT under NDCP 2018 para 2.2(g), proposing a cross-sector AI regulator (AIDAI), a risk-based framework and telecom-specific AI uses. No formal DoT acceptance was traced.
key_provisions: Proposes an independent statutory Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority of India (AIDAI) with a multi-stakeholder advisory body; Recommends a risk-based regulatory framework with legally binding obligations for high-risk AI use cases affecting people; Telecom use cases: AI/ML for duplicate-SIM detection (ASTRA), spam call/message filtering, grievance dashboards for the DoT Public Grievance Unit; Recommendations are advisory to DoT under section 11 of the TRAI Act; DoT response not located
confidence_note: TRAI press release URL located; content confirmed by MediaNama summary. DoT's formal response (acceptance/back-reference) could not be found.

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
issuing_body: Parliament of India / Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
summary: Consent-based statute governing processing of digital personal data by data fiduciaries, with a Data Protection Board as adjudicator. It applies to automated and AI-driven processing because 'processing' is defined to include wholly or partly automated operations.
key_provisions: Processing permitted only on consent (s. 6) or for 'certain legitimate uses' (s. 7); consent notice must state purpose and withdrawal mechanism; Children's data (under 18): verifiable parental consent required; tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising directed at children prohibited (s. 9); Significant Data Fiduciaries (s. 10) must appoint a Data Protection Officer and independent data auditor and conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments; Data principals have rights of access, correction, erasure and grievance redressal (ss. 11-13); no explicit right against solely automated decisions; Penalties up to Rs 250 crore per instance for failure to take reasonable security safeguards (Schedule); Section 44(3) amends the RTI Act, 2005 to exempt personal information from disclosure
confidence_note: Act text and dates are well established; phased commencement confirmed by MediaNama reporting of the 13 Nov 2025 notification. Exact S.O. numbers for the commencement notifications were not retrieved.

title: G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration (AI paragraphs)
issuing_body: Ministry of External Affairs (G20 Secretariat, India Presidency) / G20
summary: Consensus leaders' declaration of India's G20 presidency. Paragraph 61 sets out the G20's position on AI, reaffirming the 2019 G20 AI Principles and a pro-innovation governance approach.
key_provisions: Para 61: commits to 'leverage AI for the public good by solving challenges in a responsible, inclusive and human-centric manner'; Para 61(i): 'Reaffirm our commitment to G20 AI Principles (2019)' and share information on approaches to using AI in the digital economy; Para 61(ii): 'pursue a pro-innovation regulatory/governance approach that maximizes the benefits and takes into account the risks associated with the use of AI'; Para 61(iii): promote responsible AI for achieving the SDGs; Lists transparency and explainability, fairness, accountability, regulation, safety, human oversight, ethics, biases, privacy and data protection as issues to address
confidence_note: Paragraph 61 text read from the University of Toronto G7/G20 Documents Database (verbatim archive). The official g20.in PDF URL is given but g20.in refused connections and mea.gov.in's copy returned 404 at verification.

title: Anil Kapoor v Simply Life India & Ors, Delhi High Court (CS(COMM) 652/2023)
issuing_body: Delhi High Court (Justice Prathiba M. Singh)
summary: The first Indian order expressly restraining use of AI, deepfakes, face-morphing and voice cloning to misuse a celebrity's persona, name, voice and catchphrase ('jhakaas'). It established the template of John Doe injunctions with takedown directions to platforms and domain registrars that later personality-rights cases followed.
key_provisions: Restrained defendants from using Anil Kapoor's name, likeness, image, voice or persona 'using AI, face morphing, GIFs, deepfakes' for commercial gain; Directed domain blocking and takedown by intermediaries; John Doe (Ashok Kumar) defendants included; Recognised dilution and tarnishment of persona including sexually explicit deepfakes as actionable; Followed in Jackie Shroff (May 2024), Arijit Singh (Bombay HC, 2024) and the 2025 cluster of orders
confidence_note: Dates and holdings widely reported; the Indian Kanoon order was not fetched this session. Case number from recall.

title: Advisory Group on AI for an India-specific Regulatory Framework
issuing_body: MeitY; chaired by the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India
summary: Multi-stakeholder advisory group under the PSA that commissioned the January 2025 subcommittee report; the PSA later became a member of the AIGEG.
key_provisions: Chaired by the Principal Scientific Adviser (Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood); Members from government, academia and industry; Prof. Balaraman Ravindran among members; Constituted the subcommittee on AI governance guidelines development on 9 Nov 2023; Its subcommittee report became the consultation draft for the 2025 guidelines
confidence_note: Existence and PSA chairmanship reported via MeitY parliamentary reply (as cited by MediaNama); no constituting order located. Month of formation approximate.

title: Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) / UK-hosted AI Safety Summit
summary: First multilateral declaration on frontier AI safety. India signed as one of 28 countries plus the EU.
key_provisions: Recognises frontier AI risks, particularly in cybersecurity and biotechnology, and commits to international cooperation; Commits signatories to risk-based policies and to seek transparency and accountability from private actors developing frontier AI; Supports an internationally inclusive network of scientific research on frontier AI safety; Commits to continue the summit series (Seoul 2024, Paris 2025, New Delhi 2026)
confidence_note: Official gov.uk text read; India appears in the signatory list.

title: MeitY advisory to intermediaries on deepfakes (7 November 2023)

title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
summary: India's first binding AI-specific obligations. The amendment defines 'synthetically generated information' (SGI), requires platforms that enable its creation to label it prominently and embed permanent provenance metadata, requires SSMIs to collect user declarations and verify them technically, and cuts takedown timelines to 3 hours for government or court notices and 2 hours for non-consensual intimate imagery.
key_provisions: New Rule 2(1)(wa): SGI is audio, visual or audio-visual information artificially or algorithmically created, generated, modified or altered using a computer resource so as to appear real, authentic or true; text-only output, routine editing, accessibility improvements and document creation are excluded; Rule 3(3): intermediaries offering SGI tools must ensure SGI is prominently labelled and embedded with permanent metadata or a technical provenance mechanism including a unique identifier, and must not permit removal or suppression of labels/metadata; the draft's 10% size requirement was replaced with a qualitative 'prominent' standard; Rule 4(1A): SSMIs must obtain a user declaration on whether content is SGI, deploy appropriate technical measures including automated tools to verify, and display a label on confirmed SGI; 'endeavour to deploy' changed to 'deploy'; Rule 3(1)(d): removal within 3 hours (down from 36) of a court order or reasoned notification from an authorised government officer; Rule 3(1)(b) general categories 36 hours (down from 72); Rule 3(2)(b): removal within 2 hours (down from 24) of complaints about nudity, sexual acts or impersonation including morphed and deepfake imagery; Grievance resolution shortened from 15 to 7 days; removal of SGI by automated tools deemed not to breach s. 79(2)(a)/(b) conditions; non-compliance forfeits s. 79 safe harbour
confidence_note: Gazette number G.S.R. 120(E), notification date 10 Feb 2026 and commencement 20 Feb 2026 are stated verbatim in the Standing Committee's 27th Report (official text, hosted by MediaNama).
